text:
incident-bot: [PAGE] praxis-thera-prod (dedicated pool: prx-prod) - high tail latency and queue growth detected. 95th latency > 800ms, queue depth spiking. Paging oncall group @eng-oncall :rotating_light:

maria: acked. looking at SLO dashboard now. 

aj: grabbing logs from prx-prod workers, starting tail on /var/log/redwood/serve.log 

samir: can you confirm this is isolated to PraxisThera? any cross-tenant impact? 

maria: early look - high backlog on tenant queue prx:queue:main, other tenants appear normal. KV cache hit rate for prx is low (warmups).

eli: checking node-level metrics. one worker in prx-prod pool shows high cpu and repeated OOM-kernel logs about 20m ago. not all nodes affected.

ops-bot: deploy detected: model-fork v2.1 rolled to prx-prod 1805122000 by ci-bot. 

aj: logs show lots of long sequences (avg requested length ~1800 tokens) causing large batches. scheduler is grouping up to 8 requests into large batch due to high max_batch_tokens setting. 

samir: suggestion: apply immediate mitigation - reduce max_batch_tokens for tenant prx to 256 and lower max_batch_size to 4, enable queue_shaper to smooth bursts. anyone opposed? 

lina: +1, do it. also consider temporary rate cap for prx at 60 rps to prevent runaway. 

maria: preparing a config patch. will apply to tenant routing layer (no worker restart). patch: 

```
# ephemeral override for tenant prx
tenant_overrides:
  prx:
    scheduler:
      max_batch_tokens: 256
      max_batch_size: 4
      queue_shaper: enabled
      request_rate_cap: 60
```

aj: applying patch to edge routing and scheduler service now. pushing rollout to 10% -> 100% over 30s. 

incident-bot: change request submitted: override/prx/1805123467 by maria. rollout started. 

samir: also enable fallback model route for prx (model-small) for requests that would exceed 2s latency threshold. configure runtime to fallback after 1200ms. 

maria: adding fallback rule. config snippet: 

```
fallbacks:
  prx:
    latency_threshold_ms: 1200
    fallback_model: redwood/gpt-small-quant
```

eli: node that had OOMs shows older CUDA driver mismatch; I'm patching driver and restarting worker at low-traffic nodes. will drain before restart. 

cs-ash: I've messaged PraxisThera support lead (cc: account exec) with a brief: "We see transient tail latency due to long sequences; we've applied queue smoothing and temporary rate caps; some traffic will be routed to a smaller model to maintain SLOs. We'll update in 15m."

noah: taking handoff in 25m. if anything changes ping me directly. I'm watching the rollout. 

aj: rollout at 100% complete. queue depth dropping from 1200 -> 90 in the last 3m. 95th latency down to 420ms. 

maria: KV cache warmups are improving hit rate after throttling; token cost per request falling. no errors in scheduler. 

samir: great. keep the tenant override active for 2 hours, then revert to baseline with a staged test. we'll run a targeted canary with adjusted max_batch_tokens 512 next. create a follow-up ticket. 

ops-bot: incident severity updated to P2. incident channel pinned: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/eng-oncall/p1805123456 

maria: creating follow-up runbook: ticket INF-4321, includes action items: postmortem, driver upgrade plan, long-sequence mitigation doc, customer comms log. 

noah: handoff now. I'm primary until 0730. contact list: @maria (primary), @samir (runtime), @eli (infra). 

aj: monitoring will continue. if queue grows above 300 again, re-enable stricter cap of 30 rps and isolate tenant to a dedicated micro-pool. 

cs-ash: PraxisThera replied: "Thanks for the quick mitigation. We'll throttle some user workflows on our side too"

samir: closing loop: plan for tomorrow - model profiling for long sequences, add per-tenant token_budget enforcement, and add a scheduler knob UI in Console for quick temp overrides. 

incident-bot: incident closed for now (mitigated). reopen if metrics regress. :white_check_mark:"
